learning_outcomes.text: The student understands the taught techniques to optimize a computer network for different types of media (such as Voice over IP and Video Streaming) and can explain them.

The student is able to configure and optimize a computer network and servers, specifically for different types of media (such as Voice over IP and Video Streaming). The student analyzes the assignment and identifies the needs. The student researches available technologies. The student selects the necessary components and software. The student configures server infrastructure. The student configures and optimizes the computer network for a specific type of media.
The student is able to demonstrate and explain the developed solutions. The student has insight into the underlying operation of the developed assignment and can answer technical questions about it.
The student is able to document their own thought process to arrive at a solution and the developed solution in a clear manner.

assessment_methods.method: Lab (continuous assessment during lab lessons: execution, demonstration and documentation of assignments)

assessment_rules: The overall grade for the course is composed of 40% for the Theory component and 60% for the Lab component. If a student scores less than 6/20 for either the Theory or the Lab component, the total grade for the entire course unit can be a maximum of 9/20. For resits, partial results for Theory and Lab are carried over within the academic year if successful. The resit for Lab involves executing and documenting assignments before the exam, with demonstration and oral explanation of the assignments during the exam. All assignments and exams are in English.
